# Palette Vault

> A catalogue of four-color palettes with free browser-based color tools. Every
> palette is built in OKLCH, a perceptually uniform color space, and is free to
> use for any purpose without attribution.

Every palette is built in OKLCH, so equal steps in lightness look equal to the
eye. The four hues follow a classical relationship (monochrome, analogous,
complementary, split complementary, triad or tetrad), lightness runs as a
deliberate ladder from light to dark, and chroma tapers at both extremes where a
screen can hold less of it. Tags are derived from the measured result rather
than from any stated intent.

A palette's URL contains its colors: `/palette/<24 hex characters>/` is the four
HEX codes in a row, so the address is a complete description of the palette and
needs no lookup.

## Colors in depth

Each of these has hex, RGB, HSL and OKLCH values, an eleven-step shade scale
built in OKLCH, contrast figures against white and black, and matching palettes.

- [Pastel colors](https://palettevault.github.io/colors/pastel/): the soft, low-chroma family
- [Shades of purple](https://palettevault.github.io/colors/purple/)
- [Coral color](https://palettevault.github.io/colors/coral/)
- [Ivory color](https://palettevault.github.io/colors/ivory/)
- [Lime green](https://palettevault.github.io/colors/lime-green/)
- [Gold color](https://palettevault.github.io/colors/gold/): why a flat fill never reads as metal
- [Espresso brown](https://palettevault.github.io/colors/espresso/)
- [Gunmetal gray](https://palettevault.github.io/colors/gunmetal/): #36393E, the dark-mode background
- [Rose pink](https://palettevault.github.io/colors/rose-pink/)
- [Transparent blue](https://palettevault.github.io/colors/transparent-blue/): alpha and opacity in CSS, and why transparency has no hex code
- [Y2K colors](https://palettevault.github.io/colors/y2k/): the 1999-2003 aesthetic, and why it fails contrast checks

## Tools

All run entirely in the browser. No image or color is ever uploaded.

- [All tools](https://palettevault.github.io/tools/)
- [Palette generator](https://palettevault.github.io/tools/generate/): OKLCH harmony schemes with per-swatch locking
- [Extract palette from image](https://palettevault.github.io/tools/extract/): k-means clustering in OKLab
- [Color collage generator](https://palettevault.github.io/tools/collage/): an image plus its extracted colors as one shareable PNG
- [Contrast checker](https://palettevault.github.io/tools/contrast/): WCAG 2.1 AA and AAA, with the nearest passing color
- [Color picker](https://palettevault.github.io/tools/picker/): HEX, RGB, HSL, OKLCH and a tint/shade ramp
- [OKLCH color picker and converter](https://palettevault.github.io/tools/oklch/): lightness, chroma and hue sliders that mark where a color leaves the sRGB and Display P3 gamuts
- [Tailwind colors](https://palettevault.github.io/tools/tailwind/): the default Tailwind palette
- [List of colors](https://palettevault.github.io/tools/colors/): every named CSS color, ordered by hue
- [Browse gradients](https://palettevault.github.io/tools/gradients/): two-stop gradients interpolated in OKLCH
- [Gradient maker](https://palettevault.github.io/tools/gradient-maker/): custom stops, sRGB and OKLCH previews

## Licence

Colors cannot be owned. Every palette here is free for commercial and
non-commercial use, with no attribution required.

## Privacy

Like counts are the only server-side data, stored as a single number per palette
with nothing attached to identify who sent it. Saved collections live in the
visitor's browser and are never transmitted. There is no analytics, no cookies
and no accounts. Full detail at https://palettevault.github.io/privacy/.
